Sumar los tres puntos en La Cerámica permitiría al equipo reforzar su dinámica positiva y llegar con confianza a su siguiente cita europea. La eliminación copera ante el Sestao ha precipitado la destitución de Manolo González y se suma a una mala racha liguera: el conjunto perico encadena cinco jornadas sin ganar y se encuentra en puestos de descenso. Además, los precedentes son claramente favorables al Villarreal, que ha ganado sus últimos cinco enfrentamientos directos contra el equipo catalán. En los enfrentamientos directos, ambos equipos marcaron en tres de los últimos cinco duelos, un dato que invita a contemplar la posibilidad de que el Espanyol encuentre portería pese a su mala dinámica. La tendencia también se repite en los enfrentamientos directos, ya que tres de los últimos cinco duelos entre ambos conjuntos terminaron con más de 2.5 tantos. Con estos antecedentes, el mercado del over gana interés en un partido en el que el Villarreal parte con ventaja... aunque el Espanyol necesita reaccionar. El Villarreal solamente ha comenzado ganando en uno de sus cinco encuentros más recientes, mientras que el Espanyol lo ha conseguido en dos ocasiones. Sin embargo, los precedentes directos ofrecen una señal favorable al equipo castellonense: el Villarreal se adelantó en el marcador en tres de los últimos cinco enfrentamientos contra el conjunto perico. Pese a su reciente irregularidad en este apartado, el equipo local parte como favorito para golpear primero en La Cerámica. The day in Den Bosch notably featured three nine-dart finishes courtesy of Tom Sykes against Cor Dekker, Bradley Brooks against Adam Gawlas and Wesley Plaisier against Damon Heta.

"I was saying yesterday that I just need a bit of consistency back," admitted Dobey. "I've changed darts. I've gone to a brand new barrel this week. I took them out of the wrapper at home the day before I travelled, and I've felt great and produced some good stuff.

"I'm just delighted to get another win after my recent performances on TV. I've had a few struggles but my doubles were brilliant today and you can tell I've been working at home.

Earlier in the day Morris knocked out Michael van Gerwen and Wednesday's Players Championship 31 winner Charlie Manby, before beating former world champion Michael Smith.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin Suspended By Red Wings as Team Explores Trade Opportunities Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: Dylan Larkin has officially been suspended by the Detroit Red Wings without pay after informing the organization he will no longer play for the team as he awaits a trade, it was announced Thursday.
articles.body:
Dylan Larkin has officially been suspended by the Detroit Red Wings without pay after informing the organization he will no longer play for the team as he awaits a trade, it was announced Thursday.

Larkin and the Red Wings have been in a monthslong standoff after the forward requested a trade in June.

Which Teams Are Pretenders or Contenders? 🤔

Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, said in a statement that Larkin has "had enough of the situation."

TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported Thursday that "trade talks have escalated on Larkin," who requested a trade this offseason and was subsequently stripped of his captaincy.

ESPN's Emily Kaplan added that "multiple teams" remain in the mix for Larkin and that the Minnesota Wild are believed to have made one of the "stronger offers" for the veteran.

Larkin, who holds a full no-trade clause, initially told the Red Wings he would only accept a trade to the Wild, Florida Panthers or Vegas Golden Knights, per Helene St. James of the Detroit Free Press .

As of last week that list had expanded to include the Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche, St. James reported.

ESPN's Greg Wyshynski previously reported Larkin was not interested in playing for a Canadian team.

St. James previously reported Detroit is seeking a replacement for Larkin on the center of the top line with hopes of contending for a postseason spot in the near future.

Larkin, 30, is signed through the 2030-31 season with an $8.7 million AAV and full trade protections through the 2027-28 campaign.

Initial reporting regarding Larkin's offseason trade request preceded the organization parting ways with former GM Steve Yzerman.

The Red Wings have so far seen mixed results with Horcoff in his interim position. The franchise successfully finalized an extension with Alex DeBrincat, but let Patrick Kane walk in free agency and have yet to resolve an ongoing standoff with pending restricted free agent Simon Edvinsson.

Larkin started the regular season sidelined by what the Red Wings described as an upper body injury, but has since rejoined his team. He has since contributed six points (two goals, four assists) in 10 games for Detroit.

The Red Wings will hope ending the Larkin saga and getting back a potential first-line center, followed by the potential resolution of talks with Edvinsson, will help this team recover from a rocky 5-4-3 start and take a step toward ending the franchise's decade-long playoff drought.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Reigning world chess champion D Gukesh visited Neem Karoli Baba’s ashram on Thursday to seek blessings ahead of his much-anticipated World Chess Championship match against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov.The visit comes as Gukesh prepares for a defining test in his young career, with the Indian grandmaster set to defend his world title against a challenger who secured his place by winning the Candidates tournament earlier this year.Gukesh made history in 2024 when he defeated China’s Ding Liren to become the youngest world champion in the history of classical chess. He will now look to retain his crown against Sindarov, who has emerged as one of the sport’s most promising young talents.Gukesh’s visit to Neem Karoli Baba’s ashram adds a personal dimension to the build-up to the championship.As preparations intensify for the contest against Sindarov, the Indian grandmaster will be aiming to combine his technical preparation and competitive focus with the confidence needed to navigate the pressure of defending chess’s most prestigious individual title.Watch:The upcoming contest is already historic, with both players set to be 20 when the match begins, making it the youngest World Championship duel in chess history.According to the schedule confirmed by FIDE, the opening ceremony will take place on November 22, with the first classical game scheduled for November 24. A tiebreaker, if required, will be played on December 12.The match will feature a maximum of 14 classical games, with the first player to reach 7.5 points claiming the title. If the scores are level at 7-7 after the classical games, the championship will be decided through tiebreaks.The players will have 120 minutes for the first 40 moves, followed by an additional 30 minutes for the remainder of the game, with a 30-second increment introduced from move 41. articles.title: Mike Tyson’s children: All about his seven kids, their lives and family tragedies
articles.summary: Former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson is the father of seven children, including two with his wife, Lakiha “Kiki” Spicer.
articles.body: Former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson is the father of seven children, including two with his wife, Lakiha “Kiki” Spicer. His family has experienced both happy moments and deep loss, including the death of his four-year-old daughter, Exodus, in 2009. Tyson’s role as a father also features in his Netflix docuseries TYSON, which premiered on October 13, 2026. Two of his children, Miki and Miguel, appear in the series and share their experiences of growing up with the boxing legend.Mike Tyson’s Seven Children: Miki, Ramsey, Amir, Miguel and ExodusTyson’s seven children are Michael “Miki” Lorna Tyson, Ramsey Tyson, Amir Tyson, Miguel Leon Tyson, Exodus Sierra Tyson, Milan Miyla Tyson and Morocco Elijah Tyson. He welcomed his children with three women: Kimberly Scarborough, Monica Turner and Sol Xochitl. His youngest two children are from his marriage to Spicer.Michael “Miki” Lorna Tyson was born in July 1990 and is Tyson’s eldest child. She has spoken about growing up with her famous father and later pursued plus-size modeling. In October 2024, she released a song called “Love Me Again.” Tyson praised her singing and songwriting on Instagram. Miki also appears in TYSON, where she talks about meeting her father while he was in prison and how his boxing career affected family life.Ramsey Tyson, born in February 1996, is Tyson’s child with Turner. Ramsey identifies as transmasculine and nonbinary and uses they/them pronouns, according to an interview with Them. In 2020, Ramsey encouraged Tyson to speak with rapper Boosie Badazz about his comments on transgender people. During their podcast conversation, Tyson questioned Boosie about why he felt entitled to judge someone else’s life. Ramsey later spoke with the rapper about transgender children.Amir Tyson was born in August 1997. He attended American University and later started his clothing brand, Debonair Attire. He has also worked as a boxing commentator. In September 2026, Amir announced that he plans to make his professional boxing debut in December.Miguel Leon Tyson, born in April 2002, has focused on photography, videography and travel. He runs Miguel Lión Media and has visited places including Kenya, Hawaii and Costa Rica for his work. Miguel also appears in the Netflix series, where he discusses his childhood and his father's struggles after retiring from boxing.Mike Tyson’s Late Daughter Exodus and His Two Youngest Children With Lakiha SpicerExodus Sierra Tyson was born in March 2005 to Tyson and Xochitl. In May 2009, she died at the age of four after her neck became caught in a treadmill cord at home. Her death deeply affected the family. Tyson later spoke publicly about how difficult it was to accept the loss. He also honored Exodus by wearing boxing shorts with her name stitched onto them during his November 2024 fight against Jake Paul.Milan Miyla Tyson, born in December 2008, is Tyson and Spicer’s daughter. She has developed a strong interest in tennis and has trained with Patrick Mouratoglou, the former coach of Serena Williams. Tyson has supported her ambitions, while Milan has also started her own activewear brand, Milan Miyla.Morocco Elijah Tyson, born in January 2011, is the youngest of Tyson’s seven children. He has shown an interest in several sports, including tennis, boxing and golf. Tyson has shared pictures of his son playing golf on Instagram and spoken about enjoying his role as a golf dad.In TYSON, Miguel reflects on the difficult parts of growing up with his father. He describes a home life that included love but also periods of anger and emotional struggles. Tyson himself acknowledges his mistakes as a parent. Their accounts offer a personal look at a family whose life has been shaped by boxing, personal challenges and the loss of a young child.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Logan Paul’s PRIME business success and WWE career: How the social media star combined online fame, entrepreneurship and professional wrestling to build his multimillion-dollar empire in 2026
articles.summary: Explore how Logan Paul transformed his online fame into a $150 million empire through WWE, PRIME Hydration, and strategic investments, while navigating the challenges of consumer demand.
articles.body: Logan Paul’s career has gone far beyond short-form videos and social media, and his work as a WWE performer, podcast host and entrepreneur has created multiple income streams. One of his biggest business ventures is PRIME Hydration.As of Celebrity Net Worth’s August 2026 update, Paul has an estimated net worth of $150 million. It’s also an estimate, not a verified accounting of his assets, debts and private business interests. His wealth is closely linked to the value of his business interests, so the performance of those businesses can factor into estimates of total wealth.How did Logan Paul turn YouTube fame into a $150 million fortune through WWE and PRIME Hydration?Paul first attracted a large audience through Vine before building a substantial following on YouTube. Rather than relying on a single entertainment career, Paul has built a portfolio that includes consumer products and collectibles alongside his media work.Paul made his WWE in-ring debut at WrestleMania 38 in April 2022, teaming with The Miz against Rey Mysterio and Dominik Mysterio. He signed a WWE contract that June and established himself as more than a celebrity guest through his performances in high-profile matches.In November 2023, Paul defeated Rey Mysterio to win the WWE United States Championship. In 2026, he teamed with Austin Theory as part of The Vision, which won the World Tag Team Championship. Paul suffered a torn triceps in May and faced a recovery period that kept him from competing in the ring. WWE’s title records list The Vision as champions from July 6, 2026.WWE has also given Paul a mainstream entertainment platform where his athletic performances and public persona can reach audiences beyond YouTube.Logan Paul’s PRIME Hydration business is strugglingPRIME Hydration is a major consumer brand that launched in 2022 by Paul and fellow internet personality KSI. However, the company has stumbled since its first viral hit. PRIME Hydration UK’s turnover decreased from around £112 million in 2023 to £32.9 million in 2024. That is a significant sales contraction and that drop-off is indicative of the difficulty of sustaining consumer demand after a product becomes a viral hit.Paul and KSI each own a reported 20% stake in PRIME according to a 2026 court order reported in published reporting. But ownership percentages alone don't tell the story of the value of their stakes today. As a privately-held firm, the valuation of PRIME and the exact impact of changing sales on Paul’s own fortune are uncertain.Logan Paul’s collectibles and investments diversify his wealthBeyond PRIME and WWE, Paul has pursued collectibles and investment opportunities, and one notable example was his rare Pokémon Pikachu Illustrator card, which sold at auction in February 2026 for a reported $16.492 million, including the buyer’s premium. The sale drew attention to the financial value that rare collectibles can command, although the headline price should not be treated as Paul’s net proceeds.His wider portfolio has also included the Impaulsive podcast, Maverick merchandise, Lunchly and involvement with venture-capital firm Anti Fund. These ventures offer different routes to monetizing his public profile, but their individual financial contributions are not all publicly disclosed.Paul’s career shows how online popularity can develop into a wider commercial operation when supported by entertainment contracts, consumer products and investments. However, PRIME’s sales decline is a reminder that a large audience does not guarantee lasting product demand. articles.title: James Rodríguez no tendrá su despedida ante Chile: Ramón Jesurún cerró la posibilidad
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol se pronunció de manera contundente sobre la posible despedida de James Rodríguez en el combinado nacional
articles.summary: El presidente de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol se pronunció de manera contundente sobre la posible despedida de James Rodríguez en el combinado nacional
articles.body: La Federación Colombiana de Fútbol descartó que James Rodríguez reciba un homenaje de despedida en los amistosos de noviembre contra Chile. Ramón Jesurún, presidente de la FCF, afirmó que esos partidos están orientados a la renovación del equipo y que el reconocimiento al mediocampista se hará más adelante. Jesurún fue claro al señalar que el partido ante Chile “está definido” y será competitivo, con espacio para que el técnico Néstor Lorenzo siga evaluando e integrando jugadores que están llegando a la Selección Colombia. Por ello, la idea de convertir el encuentro del 13 de noviembre en el “último baile” de James con la Tricolor quedó descartada. La decisión llega después de que el propio James anunciara su retiro de la Selección Colombia hace algunos meses, lo que había generado expectativa entre los aficionados por una despedida en casa. Sin embargo, la FCF prefiere no mezclar un homenaje con un partido de preparación. Aunque no habrá despedida en noviembre, Jesurún dejó abierta la puerta a un reconocimiento futuro para James, Falcao y Ospina, a quienes calificó como jugadores que “merecen lo mejor de lo mejor”. El dirigente añadió que, mientras James siga activo con Atlético Nacional en la Liga BetPlay, la Federación esperará para organizarle “un homenaje magno”. Esto sugiere que Colombia podría preparar un acto especial en una fecha posterior, posiblemente cuando el contexto deportivo lo permita y sin comprometer la planificación técnica de Lorenzo. Colombia enfrentará a Chile en dos amistosos que cerrarán su año 2026. El primero está programado para el 13 de noviembre en el estadio Pascual Guerrero de Cali, con boletería cuyo precio oscilará entre 70.000 y 380.000 pesos, según la zona. La venta al público general está prevista para el viernes 30 de octubre. Para Lorenzo, estos partidos serán una oportunidad de consolidar la renovación tras el Mundial de Norteamérica, donde Colombia fue eliminada en octavos de final por Suiza en penales. En los amistosos de septiembre y octubre, la Tricolor empató 1-1 con México, perdió 0-1 con Paraguay y venció 2-0 a Perú. La ausencia de James en noviembre puede decepcionar a parte de la hinchada, especialmente porque su regreso al fútbol colombiano con Atlético Nacional mantiene viva su conexión con el público. Aun así, la postura de la FCF apunta a separar dos cosas: la construcción del equipo de cara al futuro y el reconocimiento a una de las figuras más importantes de la historia reciente de la Selección. Por ahora, el “tema está cerrado” para noviembre, pero no para siempre: la despedida de James Rodríguez en la Selección Colombia parece solo aplazada

articles.title: Kevin Parra y su tajante disculpa a la hinchada de Nacional tras el escándalo en TikTok
articles.standfirst: Kevin Parra rompe el silencio y envía mensaje de disculpa tras la polémica
articles.summary: Kevin Parra rompe el silencio y envía mensaje de disculpa tras la polémica
articles.body: El jugador de Atlético Nacional, Kevin Parra, ofreció disculpas públicas después de que unas declaraciones hechas en TikTok generaran rechazo entre hinchas y usuarios de redes sociales. En un video publicado en Instagram, el jugador reconoció que sus palabras no fueron adecuadas y pidió perdón, especialmente a los estudiantes. La polémica surgió cuando Parra calificó a sus críticos como “fracasados” y afirmó que algunos, al no poder cumplir su sueño de ser futbolistas profesionales, tuvieron que dedicarse a estudiar. Sus comentarios llegaron en medio de las críticas por una oportunidad de gol desperdiciada frente al Cúcuta. En su mensaje de disculpa, el atacante de 23 años dijo: “Paso por acá a ofrecerles mil disculpas a toda la gente que quizás se sintió ofendida, a todos los estudiantes”. También reconoció que debía asumir las consecuencias de sus expresiones y afirmó: “Soy una persona que reconozco mis errores, humildemente, la verdad que me equivoqué”. Además de retractarse, Parra negó haber publicado una imagen que circuló en Instagram y que presuntamente contenía ataques contra los hinchas de Atlético Nacional. El jugador aseguró que no fue él quien la compartió y reiteró su cariño y respeto por la afición verdolaga. “Para toda la hinchada de Nacional, aclararles que en ningún momento, lo que se vio en una imagen de Instagram no fui yo”, expresó Parra, antes de enviar un saludo y un abrazo a los seguidores del club. Las disculpas llegaron tras varios días de controversia por los dos episodios: sus señalamientos contra quienes lo criticaron y la publicación que él asegura no realizó. El caso refleja la presión que enfrentan los futbolistas en redes sociales, donde una frase puede escalar rápidamente y afectar la relación con la hinchada. articles.summary: La Selección Colombia sub-17 ha puesto sus ojos en Unai Ordóñez, un delantero de 16 años formado en el Real Madrid que tiene doble nacionalidad española y colombiana. Aunque nació en España, su padre es colombiano, lo que abre la puerta para que pueda representar a la Tricolor en las categorías juveniles.
articles.body: La Selección Colombia sub-17 ha puesto sus ojos en Unai Ordóñez, un delantero de 16 años formado en el Real Madrid que tiene doble nacionalidad española y colombiana. Aunque nació en España, su padre es colombiano, lo que abre la puerta para que pueda representar a la Tricolor en las categorías juveniles. Ordóñez nació el 5 de julio de 2010 en Getafe, España. Se formó en las inferiores de Getafe y Alhóndiga antes de llegar al Real Madrid, donde actualmente juega como delantero en el Juvenil C del club merengue. Su progresión ha sido lo suficientemente destacada para que el Real Madrid lo vinculara con un contrato que se extiende hasta 2028, una señal clara de la confianza del club en su potencial. En septiembre, el joven compartió en redes sociales la firma de su primer contrato profesional y agradeció a su familia y a quienes lo acompañaron en su formación. Según el periodista Juan Camilo Ruíz, la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol sigue de cerca la situación del atacante. Ordóñez cuenta con pasaporte español y colombiano y estaría abierto a la posibilidad de vestir la camiseta de Colombia. La idea de la Selección Colombia sub-17 sería convocarlo para el próximo ciclo de trabajo, con miras a finales de 2026 y comienzos de 2027. El técnico Fredy Hurtado lo tendría en cuenta para el futuro, aunque no llegaría a tiempo para el Mundial Sub-17, programado del 19 de noviembre al 13 de diciembre de 2026. Para Ordóñez, elegir entre Colombia y España no es solo una decisión deportiva: también implica definir su identidad internacional en una etapa temprana de su carrera. Representar a Colombia le daría la oportunidad de integrarse a un proceso juvenil y competir en torneos CONMEBOL y FIFA, mientras que continuar con España lo mantendría dentro del sistema de selección de su país natal.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham breaks silence on ‘hate piece’ after Candace Buckner’s controversial Indiana Fever column
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has pushed back against criticism of her views on transgender athletes in women's sports after a columnist urged the
articles.body: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has pushed back against criticism of her views on transgender athletes in women's sports after a columnist urged the team to move on from her. The debate drew fresh attention after Fox News hosts Kat Timpf and Kennedy discussed the issue with Ainsley Earhardt on October 8. The panel also spoke about public support for Cunningham's position and previewed a new episode of their podcast, the Girls. Cunningham later responded directly to the criticism, making it clear she would not let others decide what she could say.Sophie Cunningham Responds After The Athletic Columnist Candace Buckner Calls for the Indiana Fever to Move OnThe dispute followed an October 6 column by Candace Buckner of The Athletic, a sports publication owned by The New York Times. Buckner argued that the Indiana Fever should part ways with Cunningham because the attention around her public views had become a distraction for the team.Cunningham has spoken against transgender women competing in women's sports. She has said she wants to protect young girls while making clear that her position does not mean she hates transgender people. Her comments have drawn both support and criticism, turning the Fever guard into a major talking point beyond basketball.In her column, Buckner described Cunningham as "too combustible" and argued that her views brought further division to a team already dealing with intense attention around star guard Caitlin Clark.The column also questioned whether keeping Cunningham was worth the attention surrounding her. Buckner's argument focused on the effect of the controversy on the Fever, rather than simply on Cunningham's basketball skills.The criticism did not go unanswered. On the October 10 episode of No Hesitation with Sophie Cunningham & Drew Hanlen, Cunningham addressed the column and made it clear she was not worried about what critics thought of her."That’s why I literally don’t even care what anyone says about me anymore," Cunningham said. "Because I’ve said this so many times, is if you’re going to live by the praise, you’re going to die by the hate."Her co-host, Drew Hanlen, also defended her and called the article an "absolute hate piece." He argued that Cunningham's value to the team should be judged through basketball, not just the arguments surrounding her public comments.Kat Timpf and Kennedy Discuss Sophie Cunningham's Views on Fox NewsFox News also discussed the dispute in a video published on October 8. Kat Timpf and Kennedy joined Ainsley Earhardt to talk about Cunningham's views and the call for the Fever to part ways with her.According to the video's description, the discussion included a claim that 80% of the country agrees with Cunningham's position. However, the description did not name a poll or provide details about how that figure was measured. It should therefore be treated as a claim made in the coverage, not as a fully verified finding.The segment also previewed a new episode of the Girls, which covers political disagreements within families. That topic connects with the wider debate around Cunningham, whose views have drawn support from some people and criticism from others.Cunningham has continued to defend her right to speak openly. In her response to the column, she also questioned the criticism of her value as a player."No matter what anyone says to me, I’m going to continue to do me. I know what I bring to the table. It’s not always in the stat sheet," she said, according to OutKick.The dispute now involves more than one player's opinion. articles.title: Lloyd Garner dies at 54: Corey Heim, Freddie Kraft and NASCAR community mourn longtime spotter
articles.summary: The NASCAR community is mourning Lloyd Garner, a longtime spotter who died at 54, on October 28 after a battle with cancer.
articles.body: The NASCAR community is mourning Lloyd Garner, a longtime spotter who died at 54, on October 28 after a battle with cancer. Garner was known for guiding drivers from the spotter’s stand, but his impact went beyond race-day calls. He helped young racers build confidence and was a trusted friend to people across the garage. Corey Heim, whose early career Garner supported in late models and ARCA, was among those shaped by his guidance. Tributes from drivers and racing figures have remembered Garner for his skill, kindness, and the support he gave to others.Lloyd Garner’s Death Brings Tributes From Freddie Kraft, Matt Weaver and Kip ChildressGarner’s passing brought messages of grief from people across the racing world. Freddie Kraft shared a short tribute on X, writing, “Rest in peace Big Buddy.” The message reflected the sadness felt by those who knew Garner through years spent at the track.Matt Weaver also remembered Garner as someone who treated people well and brought his own energy to the garage. “Lloyd Garner was such a good dude, man. He was always thoughtful and kind. He was a total vibe at all times. He's won with more big names than you'd realize. Drivers loved and trusted having him in their ear. Rest easy, big man,” Weaver wrote.Kip Childress said Garner helped people across the sport, not just the drivers he worked with directly. “Throughout his time in the garage and the spotters stand, Lloyd was able to help guide so many who have reached the highest level of our sport. Not just drivers…anyone and everyone. Our sport is better because of Lloyd…I am better because of him too,” Childress wrote.Mamba Smith also paid tribute to Garner, remembering his passion for short-track racing and the many drivers he had helped. These messages showed how many people valued Garner both as a spotter and as a friend.According to Short Track Scene, Garner worked across local short tracks and later reached NASCAR’s Cup Series. He built his career by helping drivers read traffic and avoid danger. His experience also made him a trusted guide for racers still finding their way in the sport.Corey Heim Credits Lloyd Garner for Shaping His Early Racing CareerOne of the clearest examples of Garner’s influence was his connection with Corey Heim. The two worked together during Heim’s early years in late model racing and ARCA. In 2020, Garner repeatedly called “Crossover!” during a race at Cordele Speedway as Heim worked his way through the competition.Heim later spoke about the role Garner played in his development. Ahead of the 2026 ValleyStar Credit Union 300, he said, “He's the man. He's a big part of my development. You know, he spotted me all the way through my beginning in late models and did some ARCA with me as well.”Garner’s work required more than calling out where other cars were. A spotter helps a driver understand what is happening around the car, especially when traffic or a crash is outside the driver’s view. For young racers, that guidance can also help build trust and confidence.Garner’s family had shared news of his illness before his death. A GoFundMe campaign started by his sister, Angela Medina, on September 30 said he had metastatic esophageal cancer that had spread to his liver. The fundraiser asked for help with treatment, travel, medication, household bills and other daily costs.As Garner’s condition worsened, Medina shared updates about efforts to get him medical care. She described an emergency room visit and attempts to reach his cancer doctor. In a later update, she said hospice had been called and was expected to arrive that day. Her posts showed the strain the family was under as they tried to care for him.Garner’s death has left drivers, spotters and friends remembering not only the calls he made during races, but also the time and care he gave to people around him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Red Wings suspend Dylan Larkin after his decision to sit out while awaiting trade: 'Dylan's had enough of the situation'
articles.summary: Larkin requested a trade in June and has reportedly expanded his trade list to 10 teams.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings have suspended Dylan Larkin without pay after the standout forward informed the Red Wings he will no longer play for them, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said in a statement on Thursday.

It became clear earlier in the day that Larkin will no longer be in the Red Wings' lineup as he awaits a trade from the only NHL franchise he's known. Beginning with Thursday night's game against the Chicago Blackhawks, he will be out.

"We are disappointed by his decision, particularly given his obligations to the organization and his teammates," Horcoff said in the statement, during which he went on to reveal the suspension.

Horcoff continued: "We will continue to explore trade opportunities involving Dylan. In addition to needing his approval, any trade must also be in the best interests of the Detroit Red Wings and support the organization's long-term goals. "I want to thank and commend our coaches and players for their continued focus, and being committed to competing every day."

Horcoff continued: "We will continue to explore trade opportunities involving Dylan. In addition to needing his approval, any trade must also be in the best interests of the Detroit Red Wings and support the organization's long-term goals.

"I want to thank and commend our coaches and players for their continued focus, and being committed to competing every day."

Before that statement, Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, put out one of his own.

"Dylan's had enough of the situation," Brisson said. "We believe he's been very professional and cooperative through this process."

After requesting a trade in the summer, the 30-year-old Larkin reported to training camp in September ready to play as Horcoff continued working on a move. The team stripped Larkin of his captaincy , and the forward has since been booed during the home opener and subsequent games at Little Caesars Arena.

During a news conference last month, Larkin did not elaborate on why he wants a trade out of Detroit, only saying he does not regret the decision.

"It wasn't easy to get to that decision. It was very hard. It wasn't a spur-of-the-moment thing," Larkin said . "But I don't take what I did lightly, and I got to that point, and I'm not quite ready to talk about it."

Hindering Horcoff and former general manager Steve Yzerman in the pursuit of a speedy trade is Larkin's contract, which features a full no-trade clause. When the request was made in June, Yzerman, who stepped down from the position in July , said Larkin's agent provided a "short list" of teams his client would be open to waiving his no-trade clause to join.

Larkin, who is in the the fifth season of an eight-year, $69.6 million contract extension, has reportedly expanded his trade list to 10 teams in order to help facilitate a move.

A Michigan native, Larkin was drafted by the Red Wings 15th overall in 2014 out of the University of Michigan. He has played in 10 of Detroit's 12 games this season, missing two due to injury and recorded two goals and six points.

Simon Edvinsson situation still unresolved

Larkin isn't the only situation where Horcoff needs to find a resolution. Defenseman Simon Edvinsson is a restricted free agent and has yet to be re-signed. The 23-year-old has not requested a move like Larkin but has until Dec. 1 to sign a contract. Otherwise, he will be ineligible to play for the rest of the 2026-27 season.

Edvinsson was drafted sixth overall by the Red Wings in 2021 and has 19 goals and 60 points in 175 career games.

articles.title: Knicks Plan $5.37 Million Decision That Puts Former First-Round Pick’s Future in Question
articles.summary: The New York Knicks are preparing a contract decision that would give them more financial flexibility while leaving Pacome Dadiet’s future unsettled. New Yor...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are preparing a contract decision that would give them more financial flexibility while leaving Pacome Dadiet's future unsettled. New York plans to decline the former first-round pick's fourth-year option, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. However, the reported move would not necessarily close the door on his return.

The option is worth $5.37 million. Declining it would remove that scheduled commitment for next season and put Dadiet on a path toward unrestricted free agency. For Knicks fans, the important distinction is that a future contract decision does not amount to an immediate release.

"The New York Knicks plan to decline Pacome Dadiet's fourth-year option worth $5.37 million, sources tell ESPN," Charania reported. "This creates salary space on the Knicks books for next season and will make Dadiet an unrestricted free agent in June, where both sides could still discuss a reunion."

Knicks Plan to Decline Pacome Dadiet's Fourth-Year Option

The financial component explains why the move deserves attention beyond Dadiet's individual situation. New York would avoid locking in the option salary before determining how to allocate its resources. That creates flexibility around a specific commitment rather than guaranteeing the team will have significant spending room.

That distinction matters when discussing the salary cap. Removing one salary does not establish how much cap space a team will possess. Other contracts, roster decisions and league accounting rules all influence the broader picture.

Charania's report identifies the planned decision, but it does not outline a corresponding signing or trade. Connecting the move to a particular target would go beyond the information available. The immediate development concerns Dadiet's option and the choices that follow.

What the Decision Means for Dadiet's Free Agency

Unrestricted free agency would give Dadiet an opportunity to explore another contract rather than remain tied to the option year. It would also create uncertainty about where he plays next season. That is why this decision carries consequences beyond a bookkeeping adjustment.

Still, Charania explicitly left room for a reunion. Declining the option would not mean the parties could never discuss another agreement. It would mean any return would require a different contractual arrangement.

For fans evaluating the move, there are two questions worth separating. Does New York want the flexibility of declining this price? And could Dadiet still fit its plans under different terms?

The report answers the first while leaving the second open. It does not establish that Dadiet has selected another destination or that negotiations have begun. Those developments require subsequent reporting.

articles.title: What the Buckeyes Need to do to Limit USC's Jayden Maiava on Saturday
articles.summary: What the Buckeyes must do to slow down USC's star quarterback Jayden Maiava.
articles.body:
USC's quarterback Jayden Maiava is one of the highest-touted quarterbacks across the entire country, and on Saturday, he is going to get the opportunity to put his skills on display against one of the elite defenses.

Maiava is regarded as a potential first round draft pick, and is absolutely playing like it to this point in the season.

Coming into Saturday, he has 2,302 yards, 19 touchdowns, and just five interceptions for the year. Statistically speaking, he has all the goods, but the production on the field doesn't look all that good.

There is a bad taste in everyone's mouth for Maiava because of last weekend's performance against the Wisconsin Badgers, who just beat him all the way up.

He finished the game last week 31 for 50, for 258 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. He was sacked 5 total times, and they were all huge sacks. It was a brutal display of offense for him and the Trojans that they are trying to rebound from.

So, the question is, what do the Buckeyes have to do to replicate that performance?

It is actually a fairly simple answer and one of the reasons why I believe that the Buckeyes are going to win easily on Saturday. If Ohio State is able to take the run game out of the equation and put everything on the back of Maiava, it is a major advantage for the Buckeyes.

Removing Maiava's sack yardage from last Saturday's box score , the Trojans rushed for just 40 yards on 20 carries. Woof, that is horrible.

Once the Badgers totally shut off the run game, it was all on the back of Maiava, and the Badgers just teed off on him. That is absolutely the formula that the Buckeyes need to take into this matchup.

The Buckeyes have the No. 11-ranked rush defense in the country according to yards per game, just a couple of yards per game worse than the No. 7-ranked Wisconsin Badgers.

Once Ohio State takes that rushing attack away, it needs to become a race to the quarterback. The Buckeyes have been average to below average in terms of getting to the quarterback this year, and they have a chance to totally flip that script come Saturday afternoon.

For the Buckeyes to slow down Maiava and the allegedly potent USC offense, it will start at the line of scrimmage. If they choke out the Trojans up front, then it will be a major advantage for the Buckeyes in the pass game.

I expect a dominant defensive performance with a couple of forced turnovers to boot. Should be a fun one for Ohio State's defense and a tough one for Maiava and the USC offense.

articles.title: Red Wings on Dylan Larkin: 'That ... is a strong statement'
articles.summary: "Dylan no longer wants to be a Red Wing and he's not with us," Detroit Red Wings interim GM Shawn Horcoff said Thursday, Oct. 29.
articles.body:
Shawn Horcoff summed up where the Detroit Red Wings are at with Dylan Larkin.

"Dylan no longer wants to be a Red Wing and he's not with us," the Wings interim general manager said Thursday, Oct. 29. "That pretty much is a strong statement."

Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, told the team that Larkin "had had enough," as six months have passed since he asked for a trade. Larkin no longer want to report to the team, which led the Wings to suspend him – that's costing him $41,237.11 a day. Larkin is in Year 4 of an eight-year deal with a $8.7 million annual average value.

Larkin has a no-trade clause, which is complicating the situation. His most recent list numbers 10 teams: the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild , Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars , Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes , Utah Mammoth , Tampa Bay Lightning , New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche.

"We've talked to other teams and taken calls from other teams around the league that have expressed interest in Dylan, and we just continue to try to find a solution that fits for both sides," Horcoff said. "You know, we have to sensitive to Dylan and his situation, and and understand what he wants in this relationship.

"But at the same time, you know, responsibility to our players in the locker room, the 22 other guys in the locker room, coaching staff, management, the fans, to also do what's right for the organization."

Here's what else Horcoff had to say Thursday:

The Wings are light on center depth, and see Larkin as a valuable asset. Preferably, they want value-now players in return.

"I think the goal is to is to get players that can help us right away, but at the same time, the vision and the ultimate goal is is the long-term success of the organization.

"I'm open to all different kinds of deals, and really, we're just trying to find something that that is fair and for a return for someone of Dylan's caliber. He's a heck of a player on a good contract, and it's important for us. With Dylan, you know, he signed a long-term contract with the Detroit Red Wings , and we in turn showed a commitment to him. And when that happens, he becomes a major part of your long-term plans. And when you remove someone like that, it becomes difficult to kind of replace. So, I think it's important for for me to be open to all areas, whether it's prospects and picks and players. But I am doing my best to try to help this group that we have here now.

Dylan Larkin, ex-Detroit Red Wings captain, Michigan native

Larkin's trade demand has seemed all-consuming, but Horcoff is also trying to sign Simon Edvinsson, a restricted free agent defenseman.

"It's status quo for Simon from last time," Horcoff said. "There's nothing changed there. We're still trying to get something done with Simon."

Edvinsson and the Red Wings face a Dec. 1 deadline; if the young Swede remains unsigned then, he'll have to sit out the 2026-27 NHL season.

"It's pretty raw," Horcoff said. "I think everybody needs some time in the locker room to to digest it."

Larkin is in Year 4 of an eight-year deal with a $8.7 million annual average value.

Larkin has a no-trade clause, which is complicating the situation. His most recent list numbers 10 teams: the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild , Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars , Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes , Utah Mammoth , Tampa Bay Lightning , New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche.

"We've talked to other teams and taken calls from other teams around the league that have expressed interest in Dylan, and we just continue to try to find a solution that fits for both sides," Horcoff said. "You know, we have to sensitive to Dylan and his situation, and and understand what he wants in this relationship.

"But at the same time, you know, responsibility to our players in the locker room, the 22 other guys in the locker room, coaching staff, management, the fans, to also do what's right for the organization."

Here's what else Horcoff had to say Thursday:

The Wings are light on center depth, and see Larkin as a valuable asset. Preferably, they want value-now players in return.

"I think the goal is to is to get players that can help us right away, but at the same time, the vision and the ultimate goal is is the long-term success of the organization.

"I'm open to all different kinds of deals, and really, we're just trying to find something that that is fair and for a return for someone of Dylan's caliber. He's a heck of a player on a good contract, and it's important for us. With Dylan, you know, he signed a long-term contract with the Detroit Red Wings , and we in turn showed a commitment to him. And when that happens, he becomes a major part of your long-term plans. And when you remove someone like that, it becomes difficult to kind of replace. So, I think it's important for for me to be open to all areas, whether it's prospects and picks and players. But I am doing my best to try to help this group that we have here now.

Larkin's trade demand has seemed all-consuming, but Horcoff is also trying to sign Simon Edvinsson, a restricted free agent defenseman.

"It's status quo for Simon from last time," Horcoff said. "There's nothing changed there. We're still trying to get something done with Simon."

Edvinsson and the Red Wings face a Dec. 1 deadline; if the young Swede remains unsigned then, he'll have to sit out the 2026-27 NHL season.

"It's pretty raw," Horcoff said. "I think everybody needs some time in the locker room to to digest it."

Skip Bayless criticized the Dallas Cowboys following their 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, pointing to the circumstances surrounding the matchup and Philadelphia's quarterback situation. Dallas snapped a two-game losing streak with the victory, while the Eagles played without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts.

Bayless also addressed Philadelphia backup quarterback Tanner McKee, who started in place of Hurts. McKee finished 23-of-35 passing for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception as the Eagles fell to Dallas. His performance included a third-quarter stretch that helped Philadelphia take a 21-20 lead before the Cowboys regained control.

Philadelphia's advantage did not last, as Dallas answered with a touchdown drive and extended its lead in the fourth quarter. McKee's interception also ended a possession and limited the Eagles' opportunity to make a late push. The Cowboys closed out the 38-21 result to secure their first win after consecutive losses.

Dallas' offense recorded 204 rushing yards on 38 attempts, led by Javonte Williams, who finished with 155 yards and a touchdown. Dak Prescott completed the passing effort with 212 yards and three touchdowns, while avoiding an interception. The Cowboys' ground game provided a major part of the offensive production as the team pulled away in the second half.

Bayless shared his thoughts about Dallas' recent win against the Eagles. This can be seen in a video shared by Gridiron on X.

The win marked a change in Dallas' recent results, with the team ending its two-game skid against a division opponent. Philadelphia, meanwhile, was unable to maintain its third-quarter lead and finished the game with a 17-point deficit. The Cowboys' offensive production and the Eagles' late-game struggles shaped the outcome.

Dallas will look to build on the victory in its next game as it continues its season, while Philadelphia will seek to rebound after the loss. Bayless' comments following the matchup focused on the Cowboys' performance despite the win and the Eagles' circumstances without Hurts. The result gave Dallas a victory, but the postgame discussion remained centered on the team's showing and its opponent's quarterback situation.

articles.title: Jaissle on Newcastle injury worry and Carabao Cup exit
articles.summary: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has confirmed Will Osula suffered an ankle injury during their 3-1 Carabao Cup defeat to Everton.Osula was unable to continue...
articles.body:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has confirmed Will Osula suffered an ankle injury during their 3-1 Carabao Cup defeat to Everton.

Osula was unable to continue after twisting his ankle while taking a shot, with Jaissle admitting it is too early to know the severity of the problem.

"It's too early at the moment," Jaissle said.

"He was not able to continue. He twisted his ankle when he took the shot."

Jaissle was also left frustrated by Newcastle's overall performance, believing the defeat reflected a recurring problem this season.

"We are, of course, disappointed with the result," he said.

"It's also a bit shocking at the moment, because overall the game was not that bad.

"But it's a bit the story of the season so far, in situations where it really counts, we lack in the clinical approach to solve the situations."

The Newcastle boss was particularly unhappy with the manner in which his side conceded.

"Just think about the first one, this is again a low-risk zone where we said, clear the ball, nothing happens, and a couple of seconds later you can see the goal out of nothing," Jaissle said.

"The second one is also frustrating, because in my point of view we deserve to have a penalty on the other hand, and then you miss that in the transition to defend our own box, which is again for me difficult to accept.

"We have clear rules on how to behave in these matters.

"And the third one, again a critical ball loss when you're in possession, and the opposition is punishing you at that level pretty quickly."

Jaissle also felt Newcastle failed to make the most of the chances they created.

"These are the things we need to learn quickly," he said.

"On the other hand I think you all saw also the game and the statistics. We had many, many opportunities to score, big chances as well.

"And also in their box we need to be more clinical to get a different result."

articles.title: Dylan Larkin 'no longer wants to be a Red Wing,' interim GM Shawn Horcoff says
articles.summary: Shawn Horcoff received a call Thursday morning from Dylan Larkin's agent informing him Larkin no longer wanted to be part of the Red Wings.
articles.body:
DETROIT — The phone call came in the morning of Thursday, Oct. 29, and it was a shocker.

Shawn Horcoff, the Red Wings' interim general manager, took the call from Pat Brisson, Dylan Larkin's agent, informing Horcoff that Larkin had upped the stakes in his formal request to be traded from the Red Wings, which has been there since June .

"To put it simply, we received the call from Dylan's agent today just saying that Dylan no longer was going to be coming to the rink and no longer wants to be a part of the Red Wings," said Horcoff, in a brief press conference at Little Caesars Arena before the Wings faced the Chicago Blackhawks.

The Wings suspended Larkin , 30, who will forfeit $41,237.11 for each day he sits out.

Larkin has five years remaining on an eight-year contract worth an average of $8.7 million annually.

The news from Larkin's side blindsided Horcoff.

"For a large part Dylan kind of overcame the biggest hurdle, really, which was coming back and facing the initial (questions) from you guys and get on the ice for the first time with the fans," Horcoff said. "My initial plan was to try to fix it. I wanted to try to do what I could to keep Dylan here and in a Red Wing jersey, and clearly I was unsuccessful doing that."

The chance of reconciliation, or fixing this broken situation, seems farfetched.

"I'll say at this point is Dylan no longer wants to be Red Wing, and he's not with us," Horcoff said. "I mean that pretty much you know is a strong statement. It's pretty cut and dry."

Horcoff noticed Larkin becoming frustrated toward the end of the recent nine-day road trip the Wings had.

"The last couple days and maybe on the road trip (you could) sense that things were a little bit off with him," Horcoff said. "He was growing maybe a little bit more frustrated. But I will say it was a bit of a surprise.

"Probably the last couple days you kind of saw something a little bit different with Dylan, (and) Dylan's going to have to answer those questions on exactly what he was feeling."

Trade talks are ongoing, Horcoff said, with the 10 teams on Larkin's preferred list to be dealt (Larkin has a no-trade clause). But any trade looks far away at this point.

As for the Wings' other huge issue currently, unsigned restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson, nothing has apparently changed. Edvinsson must sign before Dec. 1 or will be ineligible to play the rest of the season.

"Status quo. Nothing has changed there. Still trying to get something done, I'd like to sign him," Horcoff said.

articles.title: Bo Bichette back, as Mets 3B to exercise $42M option, per reports
articles.summary: Bo Bichette will be running it back with the Mets for the 2027 season, as he reportedly will pick up his player option.
articles.body:
Less than 24 hours after Brice Turang recorded the final out of the Brewers' first World Series title in franchise history on Wednesday night, Bo Bichette has already made his decision.

Bichette will exercise his $42 million option to remain with the Mets, according to multiple reports. The Mets infielder had five days after the completion of the World Series to decide his fate for the offseason. The Athletic's Will Sammon was the first to report Bichette's intention to return.

With no unrestricted free agents for the Mets heading into the upcoming campaign, Bichette's decision is the most impactful from the club's 2026 roster.

Now, the two-time All-Star will run it back in Flushing.

The two-time All-Star was the club's biggest splash before last season when he signed a three-year, $136 million deal which includes options for the final two seasons. Now, he'll return to the top of the lineup alongside Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto as the Mets hope for a healthier season to erase the failures of the last two campaigns.

What was in Bo Bichette's decision to opt in

It was a down season by Bichette's standard as he got acclimated in New York.

While Bichette played 160 games, he stumbled out of the gate and finished with a .260/.312/.390 slash line including 18 home runs, 78 RBI and 76 runs. Through May, he had a .583 OPS, but he closed with a .772 OPS in the final four months. He also handled his first season at third base without issue.

With that underperformance and uncertainty looming over how team payrolls and contracts could be structured in the future following this offseason's labor negotiations, it seemed unlikely that Bichette would fetch anywhere near the $42 million he would receive in 2027 elsewhere.

Now, he has another chance to prove his past value, like he did in his walk year for the Blue Jays in 2025 when he was coming off an .840 OPS with 18 home runs and 94 RBI. He played a key role in their AL East crown on the way to the World Series. He has another $42 million

After a rocky start that saw him booed early by Mets fans, Bichette seemed to find his footing down the stretch and appreciated the accountability of playing in the biggest market in baseball. He took a clear mentorship role in helping Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing get settled and appears unfazed by the pressure.

What Bo Bichette might have left on the table

In an underwhelming free agent class for position players, it could have been argued that Bichette would vaults to near the top of the market if he decided to opt out.

For teams needing infield help, the top free agents include Teruaki Sato, Brandon Lowe, Jake Bauers, Luis Arraez and Jazz Chisholm Jr.

It is possible that Bichette could have earned a longer contract elsewhere if he chose to opt out. Instead, he chose stability, comfort and one of the highest annual salaries for the 2027 season to stay in Flushing.

articles.title: NHL Rumours: Ottawa Senators Searching Top-Six Scorer Market
articles.summary: It seems like a good time for NHL Rumours to check in on the Ottawa Senators. Between injuries to star players for the Ottawa Senators, such as starting goal...
articles.body:
It seems like a good time for NHL Rumours to check in on the Ottawa Senators. Between injuries to star players for the Ottawa Senators, such as starting goalie Linus Ullmark , and some inconsistencies in their game, despite a relatively strong start, there are some areas that could use some tweaks. So let's decipher what the insiders are saying, let's get sensational.

NHL Rumours and the Sens Could Seek Supplemental Scoring

Rumours : Today's rumours come from Bruce Garrioch of the Ottawa Citizen and also the crew at 32 Thoughts The Podcast, Elliotte Friedman and Kyle Bukauskas. Both were hitting on the same thing and player, that general manager Steve Staios and staff might be ramping up their search for top-six offensive help, in the name of Teuvo Teravainen .

Analysis : When you dig deeper, the Sens may indeed want to make a trade, but it might not even be for a forward.

The fears surrounding Ottawa's offensive depth were heightened just today, as head coach Travis Green does think that Warren Foegele will miss some time. However, an exact timeline has yet to be provided. This is compounded by the fact that their top left winger, William Eklund, is already injured , and based on the original timeline given, is expected to miss at least another six weeks, or longer.

Despite this, what makes Ottawa's situation unique, is that they do have a lot of depth on forward. So, the offensive boost could come from an internal source. Whether that is swapping around Ridly Greig , Dylan Cozens , Shane Pinto, Andre Burakovsky , or Claude Giroux in the lineup, you can tell by the name power, these are no slouches on the offensive side of the puck. One of them should be able to really get going.

Plus, the way the injuries to the defence have been so frequent, even back to last season, makes you wonder if that wouldn't be a bad spot to have an upgrade. Mind you, tonight Carter Yakemchuk finds himself sitting, so they probably do have enough depth there, despite their propensity for injury. With guys like Jake Sanderson and Thomas Chabot back there, quarterbacking the attack, it can really help the forwards produce more. Also, someone like Artem Zub , who seems to like it in Ottawa, besides how well he plays there, is up for a contract this year. He's is playing well given it is a contract year, but it is tough to say if the Sens would consider moving him, especially with Yakemchuk's development.

So, as for our NHL Rumours discussion, even though it isn't set in stone that the Sens are looking for some help upfront, just where can they look? The name that Garrioch and Friedman both mentioned was Teravainen. Friedman did say that he was told that the rumour was not true. Furthermore, it is likely he is comfortable with the Chicago Blackhawks, and vice versa, as the power play basically runs through him currently. Now, Friedman is the first to admit that things could change, and "circumstances evolve" like many rumours that end up turning into unexpected signings or trades.

Some other players and teams that could have some interest include the Detroit Red Wings, with Andrew Copp and Michael Rasmussen , and teams like the Philadelphia Flyers, Pittsburgh Penguins , and Nashville Predators, are already known to be active. Also, Michael Eyssimont's name has been brought up.

But with those names at forward, it does beg the question if whether they are even tangible upgrades to their current alignment. Especially when you think players like Ridly Greig or Shane Pinto are mentioned in trade rumours, why would you give up those players if you aren't receiving a true star, or otherwise even, given their potential. Another potential name, who is still a free agent, is former Sen, Vladimir Tarasenko. Now that might take some roster juggling anyway, given that the Sens are up against the salary cap ceiling. The other angle is the goaltending perspective, and between Ullmark's injury history, and the club's well documented issues with backup goalies, who really knows if this would be the best spot for an upgrade.

articles.title: Hundreds of fans welcome Brewers back to Milwaukee after World Series
articles.summary: Hundreds of fans lined up outside Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport to welcome the Milwaukee Brewers home after winning the World Series.
articles.body:
Milwaukee Brewers relief pitcher Trevor Megill poked his head out of the ceiling of his bus and screamed at the hundreds of people in front of him.

If Megill did that last time the Brewers landed at Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport, one day after the Brewers swept the Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, it would have been a waste of energy. Only two fans even tried to greet them.

Two weeks later, less than 24 hours after the Brewers won the World Series over the Tampa Bay Rays , a swarm of fans lined up outside the airport's private terminal to coronate their champions' return.

Two of the people Megill yelled to were Aaliyah Roosa, 9, and her 42-year-old mother Elena, who arrived at the airport just after 3 p.m.

The two drove to Milwaukee from Racine after Aaliyah left elementary school. Hours earlier, Elena called her daughter's school to ask what Aaliyah would rather do once the bell rings. She could either stay after school for STEM club, or leave and watch the World Series champions' homecoming.

Elena knew it would be. She told Aaliyah about Milwaukee's Game 5 victory over Tampa Bay this morning; the game was too late for the third grader stay up and watch. Because Aaliyah couldn't wave her yellow towel at the end of the game, Elena, a lifelong fan with memories of Milwaukee County Stadium and many losses, did.

Hours later, Elena was driving to Kohl's to get Aaliyah a World Series champion shirt before grabbing Elena to drive north. Minutes after watching the Brewers buses leave the airport, Elena teared up as she talked about what the moment meant to her.

"There was always that hope, because they came so close all those years," Elena said. "It's awesome to finally, finally be able to celebrate the whole win. And not just almost."

Bryan Garay got to Milwaukee's Mitchell International around the same time as the Roosas.

The 36-year-old Waukesha native has lived in Milwaukee most of his life, and remembers more of the franchise's darker years than he'd like to. He was DJing at the Sofie in downtown when Jake Bauers caught the final out to clinch the championship, so Garay knew he'd go to the airport to welcome his favorite team home.

He showed up in a Christian Yelich jersey on his body, a Milwaukee Brewers necklace around his neck and a blue flag in his hands, which he waved as the team's buses headed back to American Family Field.

"Finally after 57 years of the franchise being in Milwaukee, we did it," Garay said. "We did ittttt!"

Garay and the Roosas were part of a crowd of hundreds that took every parking spot in the airport observation area, and blocked the sidewalk along Layton Avenue. A crowd that drew supportive honks and hollers from people driving by. A crowd that waved flags and stood waiting in anticipation for the flight they'd been tracking since it took off to finally land.

At 3:53 p.m., United Airlines flight 3783 touched down in Milwaukee and again drove between two fire trucks who fired water cannons in celebration. Once the shower was done, fans hopped a fence at the observation area and migrated to where the buses would leave the tarmac.

At 4:08 p.m., the train of buses started moving to the road, and fans cheered each one the whole way.

Larkin, who has a no-trade clause, originally proposed the top three teams on the list below. He's up to 10 teams now. Here's the full list.

articles.title: NAU football making noise in FCS rankings. Can its streak continue?
articles.summary: NAU returns from their bye week to face Southern Utah in the Battle of the Grand Canyon, as the Lumberjacks look to keep their winning streak.
articles.body:
The Northern Arizona Lumberjacks , coming off a bye week, head to Southern Utah on Saturday, Oct. 31, in the annual Battle for the Grand Canyon Trophy.

NAU enters the game No. 7 in both FCS polls and on a 3-game winning streak. Saturday's game in Cedar City, Utah, starts at noon and will stream live on ESPN+.

The last time NAU was ranked this high was 2002. The Lumberjacks enter the game at 6-2 overall and 4-1 in conference play, tied with No. 3 Montana State for first in the Big Sky. However, Montana State holds the tiebreaker after defeating NAU earlier in the season.

See photos from Arizona football's season opener vs. NAU

NAU's highest all-time ranking was No. 3 in 1996.

The Lumberjacks went into their bye week riding their best stretch of the season, capped by a 38-25 victory over Portland St. on Oct. 17.

Senior wide receiver Joey Stout led the way against the Vikings with a career-high 163 receiving yards on nine receptions and a touchdown. Stout added 78-punt return yards and a 30-yard run to round out a 271 all-purpose yard performance.

Senior QB Ty Pennington has been a driving force for the offense. He has accounted for nine touchdowns over the last two games and the offense as a whole has averaged 336 yards per game during the winning streak.

The bye week gave the team an opportunity to address areas for improvement.

"The main message was to attack the details," head coach Brian Wright said in an NAU press release. "There are so many things that go into preparation on a weekly basis. We made a big push towards the little things that all add up to wins, whether that's on or off the field."

The Thunderbirds enter Saturday's game 3-5 overall and 2-3 in conference play after a narrow 30-27 loss to Idaho, Oct. 24. Southern Utah erased a 10-point deficit late in the game, scoring 10 unanswered points before Idaho kicked the game-winning field goal at the gun

Southern Utah boasts one of the most productive rushing attacks in the FCS, leading the nation with 266 rushing yards a game, while ranking second in the nation in average time of possession at 33:33 a game.

Thunderbirds' senior running back Floyd Chalk is the centerpiece of the offensive attack, leading the FCS in rushing with 1,093 yards, averaging 137 rushing yards per game. Chalk has also scored 10 rushing touchdowns this season.

Southern Utah junior QB Will Burns also is a threat on the ground. Burns has amassed 843 rushing yards this season, good enough for eighth nationally, and leads the FCS with an 8.4 yards-per-carry average. Burns has also added 10 rushing touchdowns for the Thunderbirds this season.

"[Floyd Chalk] is Dynamic, he's a home run hitter," Wright said in the NAU press release. "He's a major threat with the football in his hands. They do a great job up front, creating holes and spaces for him. Once he gets in the second and third level, look out."

The Grand Canyon Trophy adds another layer to Saturday's game. NAU leads the all-time series 17-10, but the trophy series has been split, 6-6, since its introduction in 2012. The Lumberjacks have won the last four games against Southern Utah.

articles.title: Mavericks’ Latest Home Crowd Hits a Low Dallas Hasn’t Seen in Nearly 25 Years
articles.summary: The Dallas Mavericks delivered a win over the Oklahoma City Thunder, but another number from the evening is attracting attention. The announced attendance at...
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks delivered a win over the Oklahoma City Thunder, but another number from the evening is attracting attention. The announced attendance at American Airlines Center was 18,111. That figure has prompted a historical comparison that gives Dallas fans something to discuss beyond the scoreboard.

TicketData founder Keith Pagello, who posts on X as @kapkap42, identified the turnout as Dallas' lowest home attendance in nearly 25 years. That comparison needs context because pandemic-era restrictions produced smaller crowds. It should not be interpreted as an unrestricted claim covering every home game during that period.

The verified attendance figure still provides a starting point. Dallas drew 19,555 for its previous home game against the San Antonio Spurs. Wednesday's total was 1,444 lower, a decline of approximately 7.4%.

Mavericks Attendance Falls From Home Opener

That is a noticeable difference between two games early in the schedule. However, it does not establish why fewer tickets were counted for the Thunder matchup. Attendance totals cannot independently explain fans' purchasing decisions, competing commitments or willingness to attend a game.

The comparison also involves a home opener against San Antonio and a Wednesday matchup against Oklahoma City. Those are different settings rather than identical tests of demand. That does not erase the decline, but it matters when deciding what the numbers can support.

For Mavericks fans, the interesting contrast is that the smaller crowd accompanied a strong performance. Dallas beat Oklahoma City 120-96, handing the Thunder their first loss of the season. The game offered a reason for optimism even as the attendance figure raised questions.

That combination prevents this from becoming a story about a team playing poorly and losing its audience. The result and the turnout moved in different directions. Understanding whether that becomes meaningful requires more than one night.

The next useful comparison will come across several home dates. If attendance rebounds, Wednesday could look more like an isolated dip. If lower figures continue across different opponents and nights, the pattern would deserve closer examination.

There is another distinction worth keeping in mind. Announced attendance does not necessarily tell readers how many people occupied their seats throughout the evening. It should not be treated as a measurement of atmosphere or crowd participation.

Nor does one lower total prove that Dallas supporters have abandoned the franchise. That would require evidence beyond an attendance comparison. Fans can question the number without turning it into a verdict on an entire community.

For now, Dallas has two developments to assess: an impressive victory and an unusually low announced crowd. The performance gives supporters something positive to build around. Whether the attendance becomes a larger concern will depend on what follows, rather than the interpretation of one headline.

articles.title: 5 stats to explain Packers' 27-19 win over Panthers on 'TNF'
articles.summary: How did the Packers beat the Panthers on Thursday night? These five stats can help explain.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers took down the visiting Carolina Panthers on "Thursday Night Football" to open Week 8 in the NFL. The big stats to know: Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes and Josh Jacobs scored twice, while the Packers defense produced six sacks and held the Panthers to just 3.7 yards per play.

Five other stats to explain the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers:

The Packers pressured Bryce Young on 48.9 percent of his dropbacks on Thursday night, and he completed only seven passes for 41 yards and took six sacks while pressured, per Next Gen Stats. Brenton Cox Jr. (6), Dani Dennis-Sutton and Lukas Van Ness (5) led the way in the pressure department for the Packers, who consistently won at the line of scrimmage and forced Young into rushed decisions or improvised throws. Because of the pass protection issues, Young completed only two passes thrown more than 10 yards downfield and attempted only one pass more than 20 yards downfield.

While Bryce Young languished under pressure, Jordan Love consistently got the ball out of his hands quick and on time. Per Next Gen Stats, Love completed 23 of 25 passes thrown in under 2.5 seconds after the snap, completing negating any pass-rush. His 23 "quick" completions were the most in a game by a quarterback this season and by far the most in his career, beating the 19 he had during Week 7 in 2024. Two of his three touchdowns came on quick throws under 2.5 seconds. The Panthers tried to blitz Love, but he consistently found quick answers to beat potential pressure.

The Packers turned the ball over three times: Coleman Owen's fumble on the opening kickoff return, Christian Watson's fumble in the second quarter and Jordan Love's interception to start the fourth quarter. But the Panthers turned those three takeaways into all of three points . And the field goal came after Owen's fumble set up the Panthers inside the 30-yard line. Turnovers can be huge momentum-turning plays in games, but not if a defense stands tall. Jonathan Gannon's group made sure mistakes made didn't turn into a run of points for the Panthers.

The Packers' putrid run game managed only 66 yards, and 18 came on Savion Williams' gadget run. Josh Jacobs struggled to get going, turning 21 carries into only 39 yards -- becoming the first player since 2023 to carry at least 20 times and gain fewer than 40 rushing yards. The Packers run game had hopes of breaking out on Thursday night, given the return of Aaron Banks and the possibility of Jacobs shaking off the rust in his second game of the season. But even with the worst run defense in football, at least statistically entering Week 8, in the house on a short week, the Packers couldn't revive the run game. That made it especially difficult to close out the game in the fourth quarter.

Converting 9-of-16 third down opportunities and scoring touchdowns on all three red zone trips made for an excellent situational night for the Packers, even if the offense had a three-and-out to open the game, an interception thrown in field goal range and a three-and-out after the Panthers closed the deficit to 27-19 late. Tucker Kraft caught a touchdown pass on third down. Josh Jacobs ran in a touchdown and caught a touchdown pass, both on third down from inside the 5. Matthew Golden caught a 22-yard touchdown pass (after a dropped touchdown) on third down. The Packers made plays in high leverage situations. The Panthers, meanwhile, were 5-for-18 on third down and 2-for-4 on fourth down.

articles.title: Kings Nearly Blow Four-Goal Lead, But Byfield Saves The Night
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Kings appeared headed for a comfortable victory before a disastrous third-period collapse erased their four-goal lead, forcing Quinton Byfiel...
articles.body:
After trailing 1-0 in the opening period, the Los Angeles Kings (4-6-2) scored five unanswered goals in the first and second periods, taking a 5-1 lead after 40 minutes.

Despite holding a 5-1 lead heading into the third period, they did the same thing, allowing the Ottawa Senators to score four unanswered goals in the final period; the game went to overtime. However, the Kings survived in OT when Quinton Byfield drilled the game-winner and held off any comeback attempt by the road team.

After a five-game road trip, the Kings played well in their first home game back in a week and a half. Turns out, coming home was all the silver and black needed to regain their confidence, as they outshot the visitors 38-22 and scored six goals for the second time in four days.

Artemi Panarin scored his eighth goal of the season, leading the team in goals, while Drew Doughty finished with three assists and three points. Several players stepped up offensively tonight, including Trevor Moore, Joel Armia, Eric Haula, and Mikey Anderson, helping the Kings win 6-5 on Thursday night.

Meanwhile, the Ottawa Senators struggled early, generating just one shot in the second period and falling behind 5-1. The Kings had an impressive night, bouncing back from Tuesday's loss after scoring just one goal; tonight, they played more physically and faster on both ends of the ice.

However, the magic didn't last long for the home team. The road team never quit and made its run in the final period, scoring four unanswered goals, led by two goals from Dylan Cozens and help from his two starters, to tie the score 5-5 and scare the Kings.

With just a minute remaining, the pressure shifted to the Kings, who were outscored 4-0, allowing the road team to send the game to overtime after holding a 5-1 lead at the end of the second period.

The momentum looked to be on the Senators' side after a disastrous third period for the Kings, heading into overtime. However, clutch saves from Darcy Kuemper, who finished with 18 saves on 23 shots, came late in overtime.

As ugly as the headlines would've been if the Kings had blown this game, especially after leading 5-1 at the start of the third period, Quinton Byfield wins it for the Kings, who survive to begin their seven-game homestand.

Not a good sign after what looked like a comfortable win for the Kings; they only had to defend and keep playing the way they were for 20 minutes, but the defensive breakdowns and easing off the gas nearly troubled them.

Los Angeles will continue its seven-game homestand at 1:00 PM on Halloween this Saturday against the Buffalo Sabers, looking to build on tonight's offensive success.
