articles.title: Five Takeaways from Mizzou’s 90-81 exhibition loss at UNLV
articles.summary: It wasn’t the prettiest game, but there were a lot of lessons to be learned.
articles.body:
Mizzou Basketball lost their exhibition game against UNLV on Thursday night. The game didn't count, so as much as I'm not going to talk up their win over Kansas State, I'm not going to talk down this loss to UNLV. Winning always feel better than losing, regardless of whether the game counts or not. But it looked like Dennis Gates was willing to make a few concessions with his lineups early. Also, Jamier Jones, CJ Gunn, and Jaylen Carey were all sidelined and not dressed out.

Anyway, here's the box score screen cap from Statbroadcast:

There are 13 players listed as having played, but I don't remember Luke Northweather seeing the floor. But there was a lot to think about, so let me try to parse through things quickly, since the 9pm tip means I'm starting this out well after 11.

My biggest takeaway was that one team played a lot harder than the other. The Tigers didn't have their full foster of players, but neither did UNLV. But you could see early the Rebels were focused on crashing the glass and being incredibly physical.

Jason Crowe played 36 minutes, Toni Bryant played 28, Aidan Chronister played 15. Those three players were able to overwhelm K-State, a team who is very focused on skill. Against UNLV the three freshmen, and not just those three but the whole roster, just got bodied by the effort of the Rebels. Lindenwood transfer Dontrez Williams, a Sikeston native, was only 1-5 from the floor and scored just 4 points, but he was +21. Mainly because he was out there playing his ass off.

Mizzou also struggled with MJ Thomas, a 6'8 225 forward who snagged 5 offensive rebounds. The same number as bouncy forward Tyrin Jones.

In all the Rebs grabbed 17 offensive rebounds, and scored 20 points off second chances. In the expected rebound battle Missouri was -5.8. And it felt worse than that.

Obviously 20 second chance points and a 42% offensive rebounding rate from the Rebels can skew your defensive metrics. But it doesn't matter if you force a tough shot if you can't corral the rebound.

If you're looking for simple keys to take going forward is the Tigers need to be much better on the glass. But they aren't giving up many blow-bys and the defense has largely been pretty solid.

They have one point guard on the roster, and he's not a point guard. Jason Crowe, Jr. is going to have nights where he loses the ball a bit more than you'd like. He's going to have nights where everything is fine. Against UNLV he had 5 turnovers in 36 minutes. Three of them were poor. The other two were fine. It's just something Missouri is going to have to live with. Because there aren't a lot of answers with the rest of the roster.

The early returns for Aaron Rowe aren't great. He played only 8 minutes against the Rebels, and that was more than he played against Kansas State. He only had one turnover, but he didn't look like a player looking to seize minutes.

But the ball handling problem also reared its ugly head against a hyped transfer big man. The next point is…

Bryson Tiller needs to understand who he is

Tiller is as impressive of a physical specimen as anyone who has donned a Mizzou basketball jersey. But he's played two exhibition games, and a total of about 50 minutes of game action and he's turned the ball over 10 times. He's also just 4-16 from the floor.

This is why in our post-Pro Day podcast we tempered some of the excitement about Tiller's play. We've seen him play a lot, and he's capable of looking like he did in the pro day. He's capable of being dominant. But he's spent a lot of time developing skills he doesn't need to be the most effective player he can be.

There were even segments against UNLV where he asserted himself and he looked good. But the rest of the time he looked disinterested and passive.

For Missouri to be the best version of themselves, they need Tiller to be a physically dominant force on the inside.

All in all, this isn't a five alarm fire performance or anything

It's not ideal, but it's an exhibition for a reason. Dennis Gates likes to treat these games like an exhibition. Mark Mitchell barely played in the second half again, as did Trent Pierce.

Gates almost seemed like he relished the team getting down and having to fight back a bit. They didn't fight all the way back, but they made a run with Jordan Crawford on the floor, and he's a guy who hasn't sniffed game action until there was 7 minutes to play in the game. Down the stretch they were fighting back with Crawford, Bryant, Crowe, Kennard Davis and Nicholas Randall. Not a complete white flag lineup, but doing the same thing he did last week against Kansas State. Play the young guys.

So again, no Jones, no Carey, who knows what the end game is with CJ Gunn, but limited Pierce and Mitchell. This wasn't Mizzou's best foot forward. I still think they could have played better, and they could have played a lot harder. But the games begin the count next week.

That's it. It's late. Real action begins next week. And we still have previewing to do.

articles.title: Musumeci’s belt goes to Filipino champ, UFC BJJ changes rules after Nicky Rod controversy | UFC BJJ 13
articles.summary: Jalen Fonacier won Mikey Musumeci’s belt at UFC BJJ 13. William Tackett, Nick Rodriguez and Ffion Davies also shined.
articles.body:
Mikey Musumeci 's UFC BJJ belt now belongs to his Filipino teammate.

After relinquishing the title and seemingly ending his serious grappling career , the bantamweight belt was up for grabs at UFC BJJ 13 . Two-time IBJJF world champion Jalen Fonacier avenged old losses to longtime rival Kleber Barboza in the gi, and won at a much bigger stage. He looked to be one-step ahead during the technical exchanges, and had multiple leg attacks that kept Barboza on the defensive for majority of the contest. After taking a well deserved decision, Fonacier now holds the UFC BJJ bantamweight title long held by his teammate, and also became the promotion's first Filipino champion .

In the main event, William Tackett vs. Jay Rodgriguez was billed as an all-action affair, and while it didn't last very long, it definitely delivered on its promise. After frantic wrestling scrambles early, Tackett countered with a slick back take and immediately sunk in a rear naked choke to force "Jay Rod" to tap. William was victorious in his second shot at a UFC BJJ belt and now joins his brother Andrew Tackett as sibling champions at middleweight and welterweight.

Nick Rodriguez dominates, UFC BJJ changes rules to ban draws in title bouts

Outside of the two title bouts, Nick Rodriguez was also one of the standouts at UFC BJJ 13.

"Nicky Rod," who won two $1 million dollar tournaments at CJI , secured another submission win at UFC BJJ. He dominated recent IBJJF Pan Champ Nata Tenca from top position for almost three rounds, before finishing with an arm-triangle choke in the final stanza.

The victory sets him up for a potential title rematch with Mason Fowler , after the pair went to a controversial draw last September. UFC BJJ also announced rule changes for title bouts, likely stemming from that very match up.

As announced during the broadcast, UFC BJJ title bouts can no longer end in a draw. If after three rounds, scorecards end up even, there will be a short, three-minute overtime period to determine a winner.

Rodriguez now has two wins and two draws with UFC BJJ in 2026.

ADCC champs Ffion Davies, Jasmine Rocha land submissions at UFC BJJ 13

Two female ADCC champions also picked up submission wins at UFC BJJ 13. Reigning ADCC champion Jasmine Rocha officially won by armbar, but it wasn't without controversy as Karen Atunes looked to have pulled a "Brazilian tap." She complained saying she didn't actually tap to the submission, but the referee upheld Rocha's win.

After the victory, the ADCC 2026 champion at 55 kg called for UFC BJJ to open up a strawweight division and give her a title bout.

Former ADCC champ Ffion Davies made her bout look easy, as she quickly pulled guard, swept and submitted Jaine Fragoso by arm triangle very early in the first round. This marks her second straight victory with UFC BJJ, as she makes her case for a title rematch against the newly crowned two-division queen Cassia Moura .

articles.title: Sub-plots intensify Blades and Wrexham's rivalry
articles.summary: Former team-mates Chris Wilder and Phil Parkinson lock horns again as Sheffield United face Wrexham in the Championship on Friday night.
articles.body:
Just two points separate Sheffield United and Wrexham as the pair lock horns in the Championship at Bramall Lane on Friday night (20:00 GMT).

The match-up pits Chris Wilder against his former Southampton youth team-mate Phil Parkinson.

And despite the new nature of the somewhat unconventional rivalry between the clubs, the various sub-plots once again make for an intriguing encounter.

"It's a tasty game," said Wilder. "It's not historical over 15, 20 to 25 years, it's a recent one, but it's gathered pace along the way."

Having not met in 19 years, the Blades narrowly overcame then National League side Wrexham in a fourth round FA Cup replay in 2023, just months before the Red Dragons gained the first of three successive promotions under Parkinson.

The Welsh side held their Championship counterparts to a 3-3 draw before losing 3-1 in the replay.

But it served as an early signal that Wrexham were determined to compete with the big guns in the near future.

"We were talking at a function last night, someone asked me what game typified the Wrexham team and one of them was the home game [against Sheffield United] in the FA Cup," Parkinson said this week.

"We lost two players through injury in the first 10 minutes, we were 1-0 down but the determination of the group in that game was incredible.

"There was a big gulf between the two clubs at the time, they were top end Championship, one of the best teams.

"I think if you can encapsulate everything you'd want in a performance, obviously we didn't get the win, but in terms of the spirit, belief and the hunger, that was all on display."

Wrexham won both meetings between the sides last season, coming from 3-1 down to win 5-3 at the Racecourse Ground in December before again producing a comeback to beat the Blades 2-1 in South Yorkshire in March.

"I watched both games back this week," said Parkinson.

"The 5-3 was probably one of the best games in the Championship in the whole season for any team. It was a great game of football."

Given the significant changes made to both squads during the summer, Wilder is not dwelling on his side's pair of losses to the north Wales outfit last term.

"We're not taking too much regarding what happened last year," he said.

"We know they've got some really good players. They've got a good management structure that I know well, and they've invested in the summer to make their group stronger."

When it comes to the playing personnel, two men in particular are likely to attract significant attention.

Former Blade Kieffer Moore - who scored six times in 30 appearances for Sheffield United in 2024-25 before securing a switch to north Wales - netted twice against his former employers last season.

Having scored 13 times in his debut campaign for Wrexham , the Wales international has already notched five goals this season at an impressive rate of a goal every 160 minutes.

"He's had a good start to the season, Kieffer," Parkinson said.

"On his day, of which he's had quite a few this season, he's a real handful and a difficult player to play against."

Ruben Selles was at the helm at Sheffield United when Moore departed the club, with Wilder previously admitting he would not have sold the Welshman had he been in charge.

Before his latest reunion with Moore, Wilder commented: "He's posed a threat for every defence he's played against right through his career, and at international level.

"He's had an outstanding season last year and he'll be delighted with the career he's had."

Callum O'Hare joined the Hollywood-owned club in the summer transfer window and is poised to line-up against the Blades for the first time since leaving Bramall Lane.

Wilder accused Wrexham of a "blanket bombing" approach to the final stages of the summer transfer window at the time of their pursuit of the attacking midfielder - who scored for the Blades at Wrexham last season.

Having praised O'Hare's character in addition to stating he "enjoyed working with Callum" when discussing the 28-year-old in his latest pre-match press conference, Wilder was eager to show a line has been drawn.

"You don't want to lose your best players, but I'm not going over old ground on that," he said.

"There's a reason why that happened. The timing of it wasn't great, but we had to deal with it and get on with it."

Eyes will at times be firmly trained on proceedings on the touchline too.

Wilder - senior to Parkinson by just 69 days - issued a dig at the Wrexham boss earlier this season when previewing his side's contest with Cardiff City.

Discussing Parkinson's assessment of Wrexham's own meeting with Cardiff in early August, Wilder said : "I didn't agree with what the Wrexham manager said, I don't usually anyway, in terms of that it was a one-sided game.

"I thought he should give the opposition a little bit more credit and respect."

Parkinson himself is fully braced for another almighty tussle with his former team-mate.

"I've had plenty of battles with Chris, I know Chris really well, we were apprentices together at Southampton many years ago when we were both 16," he said.

"We've both managed a lot of games and that's not easy.

"Chrissie is a good lad but it's always very competitive and we've had some real ding-dong battles with them down the years."

Storylines could emerge from pretty much anywhere at Bramall Lane on Friday night.

But for Wilder and Parkinson, the match strictly represents business as both sides bid to ignite their campaigns with a much-needed victory in a fixture that garners increasing attention.

articles.title: Instant Analysis: Blues Stick To Game Plan, Use Power Play Boost To Dispose of Bruins, 4-1
articles.summary: Stick play was exceptional through neutral zone; Thomas, Broberg connect on two man-advantage goals using just 10 seconds off set plays; Blues keep one of le...
articles.body:
ST. LOUIS – The St. Louis Blues felt the results would change if they stuck with their process and identity.

It didn't happen Tuesday against the Montreal Canadiens , but on Thursday against one of the league's hottest teams in the Boston Bruins , at least for one night, fortunes changed.

Robert Thomas and Philip Broberg each had a goal and two assists, and the Blues ended a two-game scoring drought in a 4-1 win against the Bruins at Enterprise Center to conclude an arduous five-game homestand against some of the top teams at 3-2-0.

"That's one of the hottest teams in the League," Thomas said of the Bruins. "I thought we played them really well all game. It feels great."

Blues coach Jim Montgomery added, "What we want to take away from it is 3-2, but we probably should have been 4-1, and we played the elite in the League. All five teams that came in here. … We played really good teams, we matched up well and three of the last four games playing to what I believe is our identity. You can see the process starting to come and that we're playing real good hockey. In three of those games, we outplayed really good hockey teams."

The Blues (6-6-1) also got power-play goals from Jimmy Snuggerud and Jake Neighbours, and Joel Hofer, despite some risky but standard – for him – plays, was rock solid in goal with 31 saves, including 14 in the third period.

* Stick with the process – Those that felt the doom and gloom of losing via shutout on Tuesday for the second straight game, 2-0, weren't feeling the same way as the coaches and players felt, and they felt other than the score, which obviously matters, the parts to the game were played the right way and if they stuck to that similar process, the results would eventually follow.

The Blues pumped 46 shots and 80 attempts at Jacob Fowler on Tuesday but couldn't solve the Canadiens goalie. They were able to beat the quality of a Jeremy Swayman on Thursday with four goals on 18 shots, and they broke their goal drought at 139:38.

"Montreal, I thought we played a strong game," Snuggerud said. "I thought we honestly did tonight. Shots didn't necessarily show that, but I thought we competed hard and brought the energy.

"… The message was this is the NHL and you're going to face some really good goaltenders. I thought Fowler was really good a couple nights ago and that happens, but just stick with our game of how we finished in the third against Montreal and I thought we brought it tonight."

* Getting two key power-play goals and quickly – The Blues were down 1-0 in the game on a James Hagens goal, and with the Bruins, who fell to 9-4-1, having been on a 7-0-1 run prior to their 2-1 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Tuesday, they were looking at a great challenge having to come back.

But using their special teams offensively fueled a turnaround, and it started with a set play off the face-off with Thomas winning a draw, Broberg attacking the middle of the ice and feeding Snuggerud for a one-timer to tie the game 1-1 at 15:43 of the first period:

"It's a play we've been working on," Snuggerud said. "I think the puck kind of ended up in a really good spot where he was able to sink down and kind of find me on that one-timer there. I didn't get a hold of it really well, but fortunately it went in."

The key was winning the face-off, which Thomas did.

"Great vision by 'Broby,'" Thomas said. "We talked about attacking a little bit more. He came flying off the wall and made two great plays. Especially scoring really early on the power play I feel like gives your team a lot of momentum. It was really good.

"There's a lot of things going on. 'Jakey' jumping off the wall. 'MacT' creating the space. Their winger comes flying out and he's getting in the lane and getting to the net. There's a lot of stuff that's going on that isn't really noticed. But they make the play happen."

Then there's the put-away goal that Neighbours scored to make it 4-1 at 12:42 of the third period off another face-off win by Thomas, Broberg driving the middle of the ice, shooting it, Neighbours knocking it down and backhanding the puck past Swayman:

"'Tommer' was great on face-offs tonight and the intensity of the guys helping, 83 and 63 on the line, allowed us to win it back, and 6 and 21 on the second goal was just real good net conversion which is something that Vinny Prospal's been harping on since the beginning of the year and that's the best we've executed," Montgomery said. "Obviously the goals went in, that's nice. Big momentum swings for us."

Snuggerud added, "'Broby' brings that energy and that shooting mentality, which is nice to have, especially with different guys in front of the net there. It's nice. Jakey's really good there. It was a nice tip and a nice play. I think kind of emphasizing scoring within the first 5-10 seconds of the power play. I thought we executed that tonight."

With Broberg and Adam Jiricek manning the points on the power play, the Blues were 2-for-3 and 25.7 percent on the season, good for sixth in the NHL.

"I thought it was a shooting mentality," Broberg said. "Take it to the net. It was nice to see those two goals go in.

"Usually if you win the face-off, you get a little advantage. You try to take advantage of it. I think we made two good plays there. You just want to keep building on that."

* Line changes pay dividends – Despite playing well Tuesday, the bottom line is the Blues didn't score for a second straight game, and the coaching staff wanted a different, fresh look.

Montgomery played Neighbours with Thomas and Snuggerud, moved Pavel Buchnevich with Mason McTavish and Jonatan Berggren and flanked Dalibor Dvorsky with Dylan Holloway and Connor McMichael.

"Obviously we get shut out twice in a row. You've got to kind of switch some things up, but I think over the lats couple games, we started playing consistently the same way," Thomas said. "It was nice to get rewarded tonight from that."

That top line needed a boost and Neighbours provided a different perspective.

"They're both such skilled players. Jake and 'Holly' both work hard, extremely hard in the corners," Snuggerud said. "They're both very smart hockey players. It's fun to be able to play with them both in different scenarios."

And the results as far as the coaches were concerned?

"I thought our work ratio together, people playing off each other was quicker and faster, especially on the forecheck," Montgomery said. "I thought Jake Neighbours did a really good job of bringing some net front presence and below the tops, grinding it out on that line. I thought that the Dvorsky line had a lot of intelligent shifts for us, which was nice to see and I thought the (Pius) Suter line had a great game. I matched them up a lot against whenever (David) Pastrnak was on the ice and they did a really good job for us which enables me to free up our offensive lines against other lines."

* Broberg continues to impact games – Broberg continues to impact the game at both ends of the ice and Thursday was no exception.

Along with the three-point game, he played 25:55 and affected the game with his speed and ability to jump into the offense after being a part of the group that had good defensive sticks breaking up plays.

"Anyone who can attack the middle of the ice, it creates all the offense (and) it opens everything up, especially from a defenseman," Thomas said of Broberg. "The more they can get in the middle, and he obviously skates really well. He creates a lot of time and space for everyone out there. It's great to see his confidence just grow and grow every game, especially shooting the puck and really attacking that middle. It takes some confidence to walk the blue line like that to make moves up there. He's only going to get better. It's really exciting for all of us to watch."

Broberg's fastest speed recorded this season has been 24.26 on Oct. 17 against the Nashville Predators, and his confidence with the puck continues to rise.

Just look at the goal he scored at 5:17 of the second period to make it a 2-1 game when he jumped into the play and took advantage of McMichael's pass from behind the net to the high slot after a really good keep along the wall from Holloway:

"I try to join the rush with my speed and my skating and help the team offensively and get back on 'D,'" Broberg said. "You see open space and 'Mikey' made a great play there finding me. It was nice to see it go in."

* Stick play was essential – Early in the game, Boston was taking advantage of the Blues going through the neutral zone and executing breakouts.

As the game wore on, you could see responsible sticks breaking up plays and turning the puck back the other way.

"There's a lot of guys that had good sticks tonight," Thomas said. "Super-important, especially through the neutral zone and on the track. You can create a lot off it by breaking up plays. I think a lot of guys did a good job of that."

It was essential in the second period when the Blues took the game over on the scoreboard. It led directly to Thomas' goal that made it 3-1 at 12:08:

"Our sticks were really good, especially the second period," Montgomery said. "I thought that was a clinic in how we need to play defensively. In all three zones but neutral zone was really important because we thought the first 10 minutes, they were picking us apart in the neutral zone and we were disjointed. Forwards weren't holding the red line, which made defensemen back off and that's why they can go east-west on us and they can make some high-end plays in the first 10."

* Thomas has a really good shot, use it more – We've always felt like pass-first Thomas has a really nice shot and it was on display on his second goal this season when he was looking to shoot and realized the time and space he had from the blue line in after Justin Barron got him the puck.

"It was nice," Thomas said. "I haven't shot the puck a lot lately, so it was nice to get in a good area and rip it. Nice to see one go in. … I was looking pass, but I just kind of (kept) skating and kept skating and eventually I shot it."

articles.title: UConn Men's Basketball: Interesting Prospect Pays Visit to Storrs
articles.summary: Should UConn add a center in the 2027 class?
articles.body:
Could Wisconsin's loss be a gain for Dan Hurley and the UConn Huskies ?

Storrs Central reported that Jack Thelen, a 7-foot-1 center in the Class of 2027, was on campus Thursday for an official visit . He is a four-star prospect from Maple Grove, Minn.

Power-conference schools did not join the pursuit of Thelen until June 10, when Wisconsin made an offer, Until then, his scholarship offers had come from Miami (Ohio), Montana and Murray State, and he jumped at the chance to play for the Badgers in the power-conference Big Ten.

He accepted the offer on June 13 and made a verbal commitment.

Four months later, on Oct. 14, he decommitted.

Over the summer, Thelen played for D1 Minnesota on the Adidas 3SSB circuit and averaged 8.5 points and 6.0 rebounds.

Those numbers, achieved against some of the best high school players in the nation, are far from overwhelming. Still, Hurley or his staff likely saw a real potential in the 240-pound left-hander.

There is no public record of UConn having made him an offer yet.

The 247Sports composite ranking has Thelen as the No. 15 center in the class, the No. 1 player in Minnesota and the No. 110 player in the nation.

Adam Finkelstein, the director of scouting at 247Sports , said Thelen is a physical post player with "real size" and a "competitive streak." Based on Finkelstein's review, Thelen's play is fiercer on the defensive end and he isn't looking to score first, although he can shoot. He shot 57% from the field and 81.8% from the foul line.

Nigeria native Lewis Uvwo did not begin playing basketball until age 15 – three years ago. And it was a meteoric rise, with the help of NBA Africa, and he moved to the United States last season to play at Prolific Prep in Fort Lauderdale, Fla.

On Wednesday, the 6-foot-11, 225-pound Uvwo committed to UConn's Big East rival, Providence. He also took official visits at Cal, Baylor and Kentucky . If Uvwo turns out to be as good as advertised, the Huskies and the rest of the Big East will need top-flight center play.

The centers currently on the Huskies roster all are sophomore transfers. They are Na'jai Hines, a 6-11, 265-pound player from Seton Hall; Oskar Giltay (6-11, 242 pounds), a Stanford transfer from Belgium; and Elmir Dzafic (7 feet, 275), who transferred from Arkansas.

Dzafic is a native of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Uvwo became the highest-ranked recruit in Providence history, ahead of Ricky Ledo and Kris Dunn, both in the 2012 class.

articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will aim for their fourth straight win when they take on the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on Sunday.

The Steelers have looked formidable, with coach Mike McCarthy pressing the right buttons and Aaron Rodgers steering the offense .

Still, McCarthy knows the Steelers can go up a notch, particularly with their red-zone offense , which is ranked 27th in the league.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I think, like everything, you look at the attempts. Obviously, you want to get down there. But yeah, the running pass, we could definitely score more touchdowns," said McCarthy in the video posted by the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review's Chris Adamski.

"But we feel really good about this week's package. Obviously, they're (Browns) a big challenge throughout everything they do in situational defenses, so this will be a great time to be back on track."

Pittsburgh will look to avenge its loss to Cleveland, 27-24, in Week 4. Moreover, the contest will determine who takes the solo lead in the AFC North, as the longtime rivals each have a 5-2 record.

As McCarthy mentioned, the Steelers will have their hands full in Week 8. The Browns are amid a resurgent campaign, with Deshaun Watson leading the charge. They have not had a 5-2 record since 2020.

The Steelers, playing in their first year under McCarthy, have been timid in their running game. Rodgers has repeatedly called for an improvement instead of always needing a late-game push or a lift from the defense.

Pittsburgh has lost only once at home to Cleveland since Acrisure Stadium opened in 2001. Pittsburgh leads the all-time series, 83-66-1.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8
articles.summary: The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins. The Patriots lost a har...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations.

The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets.

Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play

It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road.

As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game.

Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins

The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors.

Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami.

Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly.

He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville.

Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers.

It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas.

The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season.

Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions

Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways.

The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs.

Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game.

Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone.

Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13

The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not.

Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge.

The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games.

articles.title: Defending champ Laopakdee salvages 71 for 2-shot lead in windy Asia-Pacific Amateur
articles.summary: TOMARATA, New Zealand (AP) — Defending champion Fifa Laopakdee of Thailand salvaged a 1-over 71 in strong wind Friday in the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championshi...
articles.body:
TOMARATA, New Zealand (AP) — Defending champion Fifa Laopakdee of Thailand salvaged a 1-over 71 in strong wind Friday in the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship to take a two-stroke lead into the weekend at Te Arai Links.

A day after opening with an 8-under 63, Laopakdee began his morning round on the seaside layout bogey-bogey-birdie-bogey-bogey in 35 mph wind. The Arizona State senior also bogeyed the 10th, then birdied Nos. 12, 13 and 17.

"I had a 5‑footer two holes in a row and the ball just snapped 90 degrees," Laopakdee said. "I aimed a foot left from 5 feet and it went like 3 feet right. It's pretty tricky. Overall, it was a grind out there and I would take 7 under for the first two rounds."

The winner will receive spots in the Masters and British Open. Last year in Dubai, Laopakdee won the third hole of a playoff to become the first Thai champion in event history.

Three players from New Zealand followed on the leaderboard. Cooper Moore (70) was second at 5 under, Ryan Xie (71) was 4 under, and Zack Swanwic (67) 3 under. Kaito Sato of Japan was 2 under after a 72.

Seven players were under par after two days, with Japan's Taishi Moto (71) and China's Qiyou Wu (72) at 1 under. Moto had a hole-in-one on the par-3 eighth.

"I couldn't make any putts because it was super windy out there so the hole-in-one definitely helped a lot," Moto said. "It was super difficult on the greens. Like ridiculous. My ball was moving. My body was moving."

articles.title: 'I didn't feel': Rudy Gobert reacts to viral video of LaMelo Ball yelling at him
articles.summary: LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga seemed to be having a go at Rudy Gobert during the Minnesota Timberwolves’ game against the Golden State Warriors. The Wolve...
articles.body:
LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga seemed to be having a go at Rudy Gobert during the Minnesota Timberwolves' game against the Golden State Warriors.

The Wolves went into the game without Anthony Edwards, and unsurprisingly, they didn't look like their usual selves. They suffered a 119-114 defeat in the end.

Gobert came under a lot of criticism for his performance, and Ball and Kuminga seemingly yelling at him made it an even bigger story.

However, the Frenchman has now claimed that no such thing happened between him and his two teammates.

Rudy Gobert says LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga did not disrespect him

It really was a frustrating night for the Minnesota Timberwolves against the Golden State Warriors.

The Wolves started the season in fantastic style, going 3-0. Then, they narrowly lost against the Cleveland Cavaliers before suffering another defeat to the Warriors in their last game.

Edwards' absence is clearly affecting the Timberwolves, but other players in the side need to step up. That includes Ball, Kuminga and Gobert.

The viral video that is everywhere on social media really did make it seem like Ball and Kuminga were raging at Gobert, but the latter thinks people are just assuming things.

He said, as per Andrew Dukowitz on X: "Sometimes people make an assumption and it's totally something different, with the angles and stuff. There might be some of that. But I didn't feel any animosity.

"There was some frustration, for sure. I was frustrated. They were frustrated. Those guys have been great. Communication has been good. I've really tried to help them and also when you have a frustrating night, sometimes there's frustration.

"But I didn't feel like there was any disrespect or anything like that. Just guys that want to win and try to help each other out."

Whether it was an angry outburst or a complete misunderstanding, it seems clear that there is no animosity between the trio after the last defeat. Everybody's objective is to be better.

That is great to hear, as the Timberwolves need to stick together after losing Edwards and suffering back-to-back defeats.

articles.title: Jordan Love tosses three TD passes in win over Carolina
articles.summary: Jordan Love passes for 288 yards and three touchdowns to help lead the Packers to a 27-19 win over Carolina on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers QB Jordan Love connected on 30 of his 41 passes for 288 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception during the team's Week 8 win over the Carolina Panthers .

Why It Matters: Forced to operate without the benefit of a professional-level running attack yet again on Thursday night, Love made lemonade, passing for more than 270 yards for the sixth time this season (and fourth in a row) while running his streak of games with multiple touchdowns to eight. Love has quietly moved into that same category as names like Dak Prescott and Jared Goff, who can produce midrange to low-end QB1 numbers without the benefit of doing any running. Through eight games, Love is on pace to throw for 4,773 yards, 34 TDs, and 13 INTs. Even without rushing numbers, that's borderline QB1 production.

articles.title: Fact Check: Pat McAfee Did NOT Say He Would Join ESPN's GameDay By Zoom Due To Security Concerns
articles.summary: Did analyst Pat McAfee say he would join ESPN's College GameDay by Zoom due to security concerns? No, that's not true: The claim originated from a parody acc...
articles.body:
Did analyst Pat McAfee say he would join ESPN's College GameDay by Zoom due to security concerns? No, that's not true: The claim originated from a parody account. Lead Stories found no matching reports from established news outlets confirming the claim and no evidence that McAfee made the statement.

The claim appeared in a post (archived here ) by the @No3sports account on X on Oct. 27, 2026. It read:

BREAKING: Pat McAfee reportedly set to join College GameDay via Zoom following security concerns surrounding his recent appearances. Via @PeteNokos 'We want to enjoy the show but also stay safe. It's ashamed this S**t is even a thing.

BREAKING: Pat McAfee reportedly set to join College GameDay via Zoom following security concerns surrounding his recent appearances. Via @PeteNokos

'We want to enjoy the show but also stay safe. It's ashamed this S**t is even a thing.

This is what the post looked like on X at the time of writing:

The @No3sports account (archived here ) includes a disclaimer. The account profile reads:

Leading the country in the spreadage of (Parody) College sports.

This is what the profile looked like on X at the time of writing:

ESPN responded to the claim in an Oct. 29, 2026, email to Lead Stories. The email included a statement from an ESPN spokesperson, which read:

The safety and security of our on-air team, crew and fans is paramount at College GameDay. We are committed to ensuring a safe environment, and given the very real threats that members of our team face, we take issues involving their safety seriously. We support Pat and recognize the very real and valid concerns he has around safety and security.

The network also noted that the claim came from a parody account.

Lead Stories searched Google News (archived here ) and Yahoo News (archived here ) and found no matching reports about the claim from established news outlets using the search terms: "Pat McAfee," "GameDay," "Zoom" and "security."

The concerns over McAfee's safety followed his Oct. 24, 2026, appearance (archived here ) on College GameDay at the University of Utah. On his own show, McAfee criticized a university social media video featuring students making fun of him, saying it made him uncomfortable.

A video of his comments (archived here ) is embedded below:

The university later apologized. McAfee later discussed security concerns surrounding college football broadcasts, including a suggestion from a security group, made after the 2025 killing of Charlie Kirk, that he wear a bulletproof vest.

McAfee wrote about it in a post (archived here ) on his @PatMcAfeeShow account on X on Oct. 28, 2026.

articles.title: Why did Packers WR Christian Watson take an ambulance to and from the hospital on TNF?
articles.summary: Packers WR Christian Watson had a wild Thursday night, taking an unexpected trip to the hospital and producing a 100-yard receiving game.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson took an ambulance ride to a local hospital after suffering an injury during Thursday night's win over the Carolina Panthers , but precautionary testing on Watson's chest came back with good news, so he rode the ambulance back to Lambeau Field and finished the game without complication.

Watson explained the wild sequence, which started with him landing hard on the football at the end of his 53-yard catch in the second quarter and ended with Watson returning in the same ambulance he took to the hospital, running back onto the field to the roar of the crowd and catching two passes after being cleared to return from the frightening injury.

From Watson in the post-game locker room : "I think I just came down on the ball, or my elbow or something. I couldn't breathe on the field, got the wind knocked out of me. Got back to the sideline and was spitting up blood, so the doctor said I had to go get a CT. I was begging him to not make me do that, but it is what it is. Everything looked good, just got a rib, that's all, all the major stuff was all good, no internal bleeding or anything like that, so I was able to get back out there."

Watson said he has a broken rib. He wore extra padding and a molding around his ribs to protect the injury when he returned.

On the Prime Video broadcast, Watson told Kaylee Hartung that he was checking the doctor's play-by-play of the game while at the hospital. He was gone from the stadium for roughly an hour while being evaluated.

The main concern -- and the reason for a quick ambulance ride to the hospital -- was the blood and the potential for an internal injury as a result of the broken rib. Unlike a standard X-ray, a CT scan can provide a better look at the rib and the soft tissues and organs surrounding the rib, allowing the physician to quickly diagnose any potential serious complications.

Watson got the all clear and returned to the stadium. He re-entered the field midway through the third quarter.

The Prime Video team was able to broadcast the whole ordeal, including Watson getting into the ambulance after the injury and getting out of the ambulance upon his return to Lambeau Field.

The shots of the ambulance were straight out of Attitude Era WWE.

Watson called it a "surreal experience."

Watson finished with eight catches for 113 yards on 10 targets, including a 24-yard catch on 3rd-and-8 to extend the Packers' first touchdown drive and the 53-yard catch setting up the second touchdown. He also had a crucial third down conversion late in the fourth quarter, allowing the Packers to kill off most of the remaining clock before punting the ball back to the Panthers.

articles.title: Brandeis, Smithson Valley prevail in volleyball playoff doubleheader
articles.summary: The Broncos swept Pieper in a Class 6A Division II playoff, while the Rangers took down Alamo Heights in its playoff opener in 5A Division I.
articles.body:
Riding the momentum that carried them to district championships, Brandeis and Smithson Valley recorded playoff victories in a doubleheader held Thursday at Littleton Gym.

Junior Cecily Alva had 15 kills and freshman Addison Wells had 40 assists to lead Brandeis to a 25-17, 25-18, 26-24 victory against Pieper in a Class 6A Division II first-round playoff.

Meanwhile, freshman Victoria Jaster had 22 kills, and senior Emma Feomaia had 41 assists for Smithson Valley in a 25-20, 25-20, 23-25, 25-12 win against Alamo Heights in a 5A Division I playoff.

Brandeis climbed out of a third-set hole to secure the sweep. Junior Olivia Munoz added 14 kills and junior Addison Rodgers had 12 for the Broncos, who improved to 30-13 and next face Dripping Springs - a five-set winner over Round Rock Stony Point Thursday - in the second round.

Brandeis trailed 17-11 in the third set before mounting its comeback. Pieper (27-16) nearly stretched it to a fourth set after taking a 23-18 lead. The Broncos responded with a 6-0 run to reach match point at 24-23. Alva had two kills and Araceli had an ace during that stretch.

After Pieper erased one match point, the Broncos secured it by forcing a hitting error on the second match point.

"We're the kind of team that doesn't give up," Munoz said. "We've had games where we've been down further than those points and we came back and won."

In the first set, Brandeis led 14-13 before a lengthy serving run from Munoz got things going for the Broncos, who extended their lead to 23-13. Munoz had three aces and Rodgers had two kills and a block during that sequence that put the first set out of reach for Pieper.

"I think serving to a tough team like that is very important," Munoz said. "It definitely kept the momentum of our team, and I feel that allowed us to win. We're a team that has grit and we really dig deep and we want to win at the end of the day."

After dropping the first point, Brandeis never trailed in the second set. The Broncos held the lead at 8-2, 19-15 and 23-16 before locking it up with a block by Wells.

Brandeis had defeated Pieper twice before entering Thursday's match. The Broncos outlasted the Warriors in four sets in a non-district match on Aug. 25. Two days later, Brandeis prevailed in two sets in a tournament contest.

After starting 1-2 in District 28-6A, the Broncos won 11 in a row to earn a co-championship with Reagan. They showed that type of determination to win the third set.

"That definitely gave us a lot of momentum coming into playoffs, especially that Reagan game mid-district season. It gave us that mindset that we played the hardest team in our district and beat them in three. We can keep going and we have so much more potential to keep building off of."

Smithson Valley entered the postseason with an undefeated run (14-0) in winning the District 25-5A title.

"That gave us a bunch of confidence, but not so much that we're going to be overconfident," Feomaia said. "It definitely puts some experience under our belt when we go into playoffs."

The Rangers led for most of the third set before a late rush allowed Alamo Heights (29-14) to take it. Smithson Valley was up 22-18 before the Mules went on 7-1 run that sealed it.

Smithson Valley rebounded with a strong finish by Jaster, whose 22nd kill capped a 6-0 run that secured the match.

"Everybody in the gym knows she's a big hitter," Feomaia said. "Whenever we're in trouble, I know who to go to, and that's Tori."

Smithson Valley next faces Laredo Nixon, which defeated Highlands on Thursday.
